chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Isma'il ibn Jabr who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say about the food of the People of the Book?' He said, 'Do not eat it.' Then he paused for a moment, then said, 'Do not eat it.' Then he paused for a moment, then said, 'Do not eat it, and do not leave it; you say it is forbidden, but you leave it to purify yourself from it, for in their vessels there is wine and pork.'

key_terms.تَتَنَزَّهُ عَنْهُ: Purify yourself from it / abstain for purity
key_terms.طَعَامُ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: Food of the People of the Book

ai.seo_question: Why does the Imam advise against eating the food of the People of the Book if it is not strictly haram?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that abstaining from the food of the People of the Book is a voluntary act of self-purification (tatanazzuhu) rather than a strict prohibition (haram), addressing the practical concern of residual wine and pork in their vessels. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential distinction between intrinsic impurity and precautionary avoidance, emphasizing spiritual cleanliness over legal obligation. The emphasis on the vessels highlights the historical context where shared dining ware often retained traces of non-halal substances, necessitating careful discernment by the faithful.
